To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

MMC are present in the PB and BM of 50–70% of patients with localized PC, that MMC are not detectable in the PB of patients with advanced PC, that MMC in the PB and the BM are not related to clinical stage or PSA level at diagnosis, that MMC in PB and BM are not related, that MMC are detectable in the BM of patients with PC but not in the BM of age-matched controls, and that MMC in BM are related to histologic grade.

(i) MMC are present in the peripheral blood and bone marrow in patients with localized and metastatic prostate cancer; (ii) MMC are present before radical therapy and may be detected in patients with low serum PSA levels; (iii) MMC are present after radical therapy in a significant proportion of patients and may predict disease progression; and (iv) MMC are present at the time of diagnosis in a significant proportion (30–40%) of patients with localized prostate cancers.

the presence of MMC in PB and BM is a strong prognostic factor for disease progression in patients with localized PC, but the presence of MMC does not seem to be associated with the risk of local recurrence.
In summary, our research is concerned with

three main topics: 1) the clinical relevance of MMC in PB and BM in patients with localized PC, 2) the detection of MMC in PB, BM and lymph nodes (LN) in patients with metastatic PC and, 3) the clinical significance of MMC in PB in patients with metastases.
the question whether MMC in the PB and BM can be detected by means of monoclonal antibody (MAb) techniques and whether the detection rate is related to tumour stage and grade.
the detection and quantification of MMC in the PB and BM of patients with PC and with the identification of prognostic factors for the presence of such cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of MMC in PB or BM is not a prognostic factor for distant metastasis or death in localized PC (3).
MMC in PB and BM are present in patients with localized PC and that the presence of MMC may be associated with the clinical course of the disease.
the presence of MMC in PB and BM is associated with an increased risk of relapse and a poor prognosis in PC (3–6).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we were the first to describe the presence of MMC in the PB of patients with prostate cancer and we have developed a sensitive immunological method to detect these cells.
the detection of MMC in PB or BM is of limited clinical value in the staging of localized PC (3).
the presence of MMC is a strong indicator for an unfavourable prognosis in patients with PC (3).
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have a new tool to look at the metastatic potential of prostate cancer.
the presence of micrometastases (MM) in BM is associated with a higher risk of biochemical relapse and clinical progression in prostate cancer patients treated with radical treatment.
the presence of MMC in the PB and BM is a significant prognostic factor in PC patients, and that the presence of PB MMC in particular may be used as a prognostic marker for the outcome of PC.
